note: Canonical coordinate contract for the IRX visual asset system. compose_frame.py reads ONLY this file to place assets. If a frame needs an offset that is not in here, the contract is wrong — fix the contract, not the frame.

canvas.rationale: Phase 1 defines no canvas. 16:9 chosen for the investor demo surface (ScenarioDemo + deck). Mobile crops to a 4:5 safe area, documented below.

safeArea.note: Anything narratively load-bearing must sit inside mobile_4_5. Slot 'centre' is centred within it.

layerNote: Phase 1 established no layer convention, so the Phase 2A brief's list is adopted with changes forced by the artwork: (1) character_face/character_hair are NOT separate top-level layers - a register is one atomic swappable unit and splitting it would let face and hair desynchronise; (2) 'furniture' sits AFTER character_head so the counter occludes the figure below counter height; (3) 'character_front' (hands) sits after 'prop' so hands rest on the counter surface; (4) ADDED IN QA: 'character_contact' between prop and character_front carries contact shadows. Without it the figure read as pasted onto the background. 'character_back' carries the figure's cast shadow on the wall.

basePoint.note: bottom-centre; lands on the scene slot anchor

character.note: DEPRECATED as a global. Retained for backward compatibility with existing frames; new work should read anchors.characters[<base>]. neckSpan was never global - it is derived from a specific figure's neck geometry, and figure_b will differ. Generalised at the start of 2B, before a second character existed to break it.

register.note: A register may apply its own rotation about neckAnchor (declared as data-register-rotate on the root <g>). Rotation about the anchor keeps the join mechanical while allowing head tilt to carry part of the register.

rotateLimit.note: Rotation is TILT only. It cannot produce yaw. A turned head must be redrawn in the register, not rotated.

register.neckSpanNote: Per-character; see anchors.characters[<base>].neckSpan. Rotation remains global and is TILT only, bounded by rotateLimit.

bubbles.note: LOCKED: rounded balloon with a tail to the speaker (design variant 1). Bubbles are GENERATED from render_blocks.json at compose time - they are not an asset file. Geometry lives here; the renderer is build_bubbles() in compose_frame.py. Enable per frame with `bubblesFrom: <node>` and compose with --bubbles.
bubbles.typeScaleNote: Type is sized against the DEVICE, not the canvas. The artwork is contained 16:9 in a ~390pt phone width, so the canvas-to-device factor is 0.244 and the previous fontSize 26 rendered at 6.3pt - roughly half a legible size. 47 renders at 11.5pt. maxWidth grew and every placement origin moved left in step, because a wider balloon at the old x=250/292 origin would have crossed the centre-slot figure at x=664. paddingY, firstBaseline and tailInset were hard-coded in build_bubbles() as 34/40/26; they are contract values now so the balloon scales with the type instead of splitting from it.

placement.note: Per-slot stack origin. Explicit rather than computed: the free area in a room is a compositional fact about that room, not something derivable from the slot alone. Each new environment must declare placements for the slots it uses.

tailTarget.note: Offset from the speaker's resolved head socket to the tail apex - chin/neck height, just inside the near cheek. Resolved through the same slot transform as the figure, so the tail tracks the speaker at any slot without hand-placement.

tail.note: Length is CLAMPED. The tail aims at the speaker but stops short; an unclamped tail becomes a thin spike across the artwork, which is what made variant 1 read badly in the first design pass. Drawn on the last bubble only - a tail per bubble reads as noise.

bubbles.placementNote: Global defaults live in bubbles.placement. A scene may override them via scenes.<id>.bubblePlacement.<slot> when its free area differs - where a bubble can sit is a compositional fact about the room, not a property of the slot.

environmentContract.rule: EVERY IRX environment must provide an occluding surface at y=600. This is not a stylistic preference - both figure bodies are drawn with arms reaching forward and hands flat at local y~500, which resolves to canvas y~600. A room with no surface there leaves the hands floating in mid-air. The surface can be anything plausible for the room (counter, console table, cafe table, low wall, bar) but it must exist and it must sit at 600.
environmentContract.discovered: 2B.3, before flat_hallway was drawn. scene.kitchen satisfied it by accident because the counter was designed first and the figure was fitted to it.
environmentContract.alternative: If a future scene genuinely cannot have a surface there, it needs an arms-down body variant - which is what figure_a_rear and figure_b_rear already are. Do not solve it by moving the occlusion line per scene; that would desynchronise the hands from every existing wardrobe.

propsRemoved.prop.jacket_worn: NOT A PROP. Used by one node (confession_guarded) where Jessica's wardrobe is already `coat` - the jacket she is reaching for is the garment she is wearing. Reclassified as wardrobe-provided; mapping.the_secret.json should move 'jacket' to unrenderableProps.

montage.note: Montage is a first-class presentation mode, not a scene with the figure removed. Panels are reduced-fidelity vignettes on a dark matte, so compressed time reads differently from present tense without a caption having to say so.

propAnchorRule: Every prop declares defaultAnchor per scene. Composers must use it rather than assigning anchors positionally - the full-scenario audit caught prop.jacket_chair placed on a worktop because a round-robin had put the second prop at the second anchor.
scenesBubbleNote: None of the five Career scenes declares bubblePlacement, because mapping.the_instruction.json sets textLayer 'native' and no Career node composes a balloon. If bubbles are ever enabled for this district, each of these five needs a placement block for the slots it uses, and the global defaults in anchors.bubbles.placement are NOT safe to inherit — they were measured against Neighbourhood rooms.
